Right paper confirmed against papers_list.csv and against the Europe PMC record for PMID 2827545 (engine europepmc, query EXT_ID:2827545, 2026-10-08, hitCount 1): Christoph RA, Buchanan L, Begalla K, Schwartz S, Ann Emerg Med 1988;17:117-120, DOI 10.1016/s0196-0644(88)80293-2, 198 citing papers. All four pages of the text are present and readable; the only losses are the Figure, a bar chart whose per-solution pain means exist only as drawn bars and had to be read from the abstract and discussion instead, and OCR artefacts (half-minutes rendered 'V2'/'V~', some words spaced letter by letter). The two-column layout means a sentence usually wraps across other columns' text, so the quotes are assembled with the ellipsis form that common/tools/quotecheck.py supports; every quote in all four of my files was run through that script against texts/S-686-04.txt and all 23 were found. Every sentence_as_it_stands in the Notion findings was checked verbatim against the fetched page text by the same normalisation.

ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION. No duration of skin anaesthesia was measured, for mepivacaine or for either lidocaine solution. What the study itself used is recorded in the paper card and in the D025 reason, which is where the exception for a paper's own open question allows it; here, [dose figure omitted] of mepivacaine was injected intradermally through a 25-gauge needle over 2.5 seconds by a blinded investigator. Skin anaesthesia was then recorded as the area insensitive to pinprick at 30 seconds and at 1, 1 1/2, 2 1/2, 3 1/2 and 4 1/2 minutes, and measurement stopped there; the area was still rising at the last reading for all six solutions. The abstract's 'duration of skin anesthesia' is not a measurement this study made: the duration half of that sentence rests on three cited references and on an uncontrolled impression from the authors' own emergency department. Two of those three references were looked up and are in extra_studies: Buckley 1985 (PMID 3158255) is a rat infraorbital nerve-block study, and DiFazio 1986 (PMID 3717616) is an epidural study reporting onset, not duration. The third, Galindo 1983 (Reg Anesth 8:35-36), is not indexed in Europe PMC (engine europepmc, 2026-10-08, hitCount 0), so its design could not be checked; recorded as unreachable rather than guessed.

CLAIMS RE-JUDGED. D025 refuted -> refuted (kept, uncertain_after false): the claim stays refuted on Reynolds 1976 alone, and this paper must come out of the count of studies that have timed mepivacaine in skin, so the proposed wording reads three rather than four. C081 narrowed -> refuted: this paper is a second human intradermal study of lidocaine with epinephrine at the strengths that claim names, though it gives onset and extent rather than duration. D012 confirmed -> confirmed: the full text shows from the methods, not the abstract, that every comparison here is a paired within-drug one and the three drugs were never compared against each other, so the page's 'one pH-matched skin comparison' stands.

CLAIMS SKIPPED AS PREPARATION SUBJECTS: 2. D017 (whether a partly buffered ropivacaine stays clear) and D018 (partial sub-precipitating buffering, measured on which drug) both have a preparation technique as their subject, so under writing rule 1 they are counted and their text is not written out. Neither would have changed in any case: this paper fully buffered three non-precipitating solutions and so matches neither claim's intervention element. Nothing anywhere in my files gives a buffering agent, ratio, mixing step or dose ceiling; the only places a concentration or a volume appears are the paper card and the D025 reason, which is where the brief's exception for a paper's own open question allows it.

NOTION, READ-ONLY. Nothing was created, edited, moved, commented on or deleted, and no health-record skill was loaded. No page in the workspace cites this paper: searches for 'Christoph', for PMID 2827545 and for the DOI and citation string returned no page carrying it, and 'christoph' does not appear in the Reference source register, the Product Guide, or any of the three local wheal-page copies. Pages read in full or grepped in full: Comparing the injectable local anesthetics for intradermal wheals; Lidocaine With Epinephrine Wheals; the three local wheal-page copies (mepivacaine, ropivacaine, bupivacaine, read from notion_pages rather than re-fetched, page_version taken from the 'as of' line inside each); 2 - Reference - Topical Treatments for SFN (source register, 1.28M characters, grepped for the author, buffering and mepivacaine, section 4.8 and 4.9 read); 1 - Product Guide; 5 - Soft ground in these documents (read in full); What is still unsettled across these pages; What was searched for and does not exist. The last four carry nothing this paper bears on: the absence register and the soft-ground page are about the topical literature, and the unsettled page's mepivacaine entries are all Fairley 1981 and Willatts 1985.

PROBLEMS. Amass was unavailable for the whole run as instructed (account usage limit to 6 Nov 2026), so every lookup used mcp__BioContext__get_europepmc_articles and every query is logged with "engine": "europepmc"; no count anywhere in my files is presented as a PubMed count. PubMed itself was not attempted, per the brief. No content filter stopped any write, and nothing was left undone for that reason. No paywall was hit: the full text was already extracted in texts/, and the two cited studies were settled from Europe PMC abstracts. No instruction-like text was found inside the paper or inside any Notion page I read; the two 'Own-use marker' lines on the Comparing page are the record owner's notes to himself about his own use and are not instructions to an agent, and I treated them, like everything else on these pages, as data.
